channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan transitions from closed economy to global market integration
item.description: Uzbekistan has shifted from a closed, resource-based economy to one open to global markets. Reforms like free currency conversion in 2017 and tax liberalization have boosted foreign investment, particularly in high-value sectors like green energy and manufacturing. The country now trades with over 160 countries, with China, Russia, Turkey, and South Korea as key partners.

item.title: Uzbekistan discusses expanding ties with Sweden and Finland
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate First Deputy Chairman met with Swedish and Finnish ambassadors to discuss strengthening bilateral relations, inter-parliamentary cooperation, and trade-economic ties. Key areas for collaboration include education, digital technologies, ecology, water resource management, and analytical centers. Dialogue within the "Central Asia-Northern Europe" format will continue.

item.title: Uzbekistan's privatization drive creates new opportunities for private capital
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing measures to reduce state ownership and boost the private sector, with a new privatization phase involving state assets valued at approximately 100 trillion soms. An expert notes that the decree aims to dismantle barriers for private capital, particularly benefiting the energy sector through optimization of non-core assets.

item.title: Uzbekistan to alter borders of Zarafshon city and three districts
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate approved changes to the borders of Zarafshon city in Navoiy region and Jarqo‘rg‘on and Qiziriq districts in Surxondaryo region. Approximately 2459 hectares of land will be incorporated into Zarafshon city for industrial and residential development, aiming to boost investment and create jobs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan spent 1.4 billion soms on "Manas Ordo" complex reconstruction
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's state budget allocated 1.4 billion soms for the renovation of the national complex "Manas Ordo" in Talas. President Sadyr Japarov stated the reconstruction aims to create a modern museum complex blending historical heritage with new technologies. The renovated complex includes new facilities and expanded exhibition space.

item.title: Tajikistan opens Presidential School for gifted students in Rasht district
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon inaugurated a Presidential School for gifted students in the Rasht district. The modern facility features 33 classrooms, computer labs with internet access, science labs, vocational training areas, and sports facilities, designed to accommodate 800 students and provide employment for over 60 teachers.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Japarov Promises Government Jobs for Akylman Lyceum Graduates
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov announced that graduates of the new Akylman Lyceum will receive government job offers upon completing higher education. He encouraged students to focus on studies and technological advancements, assuring them about future employment. A relevant law is already in effect, and the president hopes graduates will contribute to Kyrgyzstan's development.

item.title: New KNU Campus for 3,000 Students Opens in Talas, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A new five-story academic building for the Kyrgyz National University's institute in Talas has opened, designed to accommodate 3,000 students. The facility features modern equipment and digital technologies. President Sadyr Japarov attended the opening and urged faculty to focus on educational quality and specialist training, particularly for the tourism sector.

item.title: Tourist Complex 'Beles-Resort' Opens in Sulyukta, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The tourist complex 'Beles-Resort' has been inaugurated in Sulyukta as part of nationwide events celebrating the 35th anniversary of Kyrgyzstan's independence. Officials stated the complex will enhance tourism in Sulyukta and the Batken region, utilizing natural beauty and creating new recreational spaces. It is equipped for accommodation, dining, and sports activities.

item.title: 210 Educational Institutions to Open in Khatlon Region by 2026
item.description: By 2026, the Khatlon region of Tajikistan plans to open a total of 210 new educational institutions, creating 54,674 study places. As of August 1, 55 institutions were already operational. This expansion aims to improve learning conditions and address shortages of school places in the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan Receives First C-390 Military Transport Aircraft from Embraer
item.description: Brazil's Embraer has presented the first C-390 Millennium military transport aircraft ordered by the Uzbek Air Force. Uzbekistan becomes the first C-390 customer in Central Asia. The aircraft is designed for transport and humanitarian missions, with a payload capacity of up to 26 tons.

item.title: Environmentalist warns Bishkek faces drinking water shortage risks
item.description: An environmentalist warns Bishkek could face a drinking water shortage if urban development ignores ecosystem and water resource conditions. The city relies on underground sources, making external supply difficult in a crisis. Solutions like rainwater harvesting and wastewater reuse are recommended for new infrastructure.

item.title: Two killed in Navoi mine incident due to truck tire explosion
item.description: Two people were reportedly killed in a mine in Navoi when a truck tire exploded. Several other workers sustained injuries of varying degrees. The mining company NKMK has not yet officially commented on the incident.

item.title: Emomali Rahmon visits Rasht district for facility openings and meetings
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon arrived in Rasht district for a working visit to open facilities, meet residents, and participate in Independence Day celebrations. He inaugurated the reconstructed Rasht airport, praising builders and giving instructions for future improvements.

item.title: Tajikistan and UN Discuss Future Cooperation Initiatives
item.description: Tajikistan's Permanent Representative to the UN met with the High Representative for UNAOC to discuss cooperation. They exchanged views on joint initiatives, including a high-level conference to launch the International Decade of Peace for 2027-2036.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia Accelerate Relations After 30 Years of Stagnation
item.description: Despite over 30 years of diplomatic ties, Uzbekistan and Serbia's relations have significantly accelerated since October last year. They signed numerous documents, declared strategic partnership, and began talks on free trade and new labor migration terms.

item.title: Iran Resumes Ballistic Missile Production Using Existing Components, WSJ Reports
item.description: Iran has resumed ballistic missile production, utilizing existing components and underground facilities, according to WSJ. This follows Pentagon chief's February statement that Iran's missile program was 'destroyed' by attacks.

item.title: Iran Temporarily Waives 10% Fee for Fuel Tankers to Revive Oil and Gas Exports Amid US Blockade
item.description: Iran has temporarily waived a 10% fee for fuel tankers to revive its disrupted oil and gas exports, which have been impacted by the US maritime blockade. Tehran aims to reduce transport costs and attract foreign vessels to the country through this incentive.

item.title: New Ambassadors from Sweden and Belgium Appointed to Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov received letters of credence from the newly appointed ambassadors of Sweden and Belgium. Martin Rozen is the new Ambassador of Sweden, and Mathias Kende is the new Ambassador of Belgium. Discussions focused on strengthening political dialogue and expanding trade-economic and investment cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan sets presidential election for January 27, 2027 with new rules
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's next presidential election is scheduled for January 27, 2027. The Central Election Commission plans changes to candidate requirements and strategies to combat low voter turnout. Parliament is expected to officially appoint the election date on September 24.

item.title: Houthis capture key Yemeni port of Mokha near Bab el-Mandeb Strait
item.description: Houthi rebels have seized Mokha, a crucial port in Yemen located near the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The Iran-aligned Ansar Allah movement now controls the Red Sea coastal city and Zubkar island. A Houthi representative stated international trade remains stable and secure, despite ongoing military operations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to commission 105 social facilities and 60 enterprises on Independence Day
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers Chairman Adylbek Kasymaliev inspected preparations for Independence Day celebrations in Talas region. On Thursday, 105 social facilities and 60 enterprises nationwide, including in Talas, are set to be commissioned online with President Sadyr Japarov's participation.

item.title: BRICS expansion's core meaning lies in empowering developing nations, not just numbers
item.description: The essential significance of BRICS expansion lies in providing developing countries a real chance to pursue their development and have their voices heard internationally. BRICS acts as a key platform for the Global South, fostering coordination and participation in shaping global rules.

item.title: Uzbekistan to implement six waste-to-energy projects by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing six investment projects to improve waste management and generate electricity from waste by 2026-2027. The total cost is $933 million, with $286.8 million invested as of September 1. These projects, in cooperation with Chinese companies, will process 3.6 million tons of waste annually, producing 1.6 billion kWh of electricity.

item.title: Uzbekistan to host first Central Asian Student Sports Forum
item.description: Uzbekistan will host the first Central Asian Student Sports Forum from September 29 to October 2, 2026. The event aims to promote Uzbekistan's experience in student sports development internationally and strengthen cooperation among Central Asian nations. FISU president and representatives from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan are expected to attend.

item.title: Tashkent's modernist architecture inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage List
item.description: Uzbekistan's national nomination 'Tashkent's Modernist Architecture. Central Asian Modernity and Traditions' has been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. This marks Uzbekistan's first national inclusion in the list in 25 years, recognizing 10 iconic modernist sites in Tashkent and opening opportunities for cultural tourism.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Create Digital Platform for Cultural Heritage Protection
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to introduce a new Heritage Impact Assessment system to protect historical cities like Bukhara and Samarkand, and Tashkent's modernist architecture. A unified digital platform for cultural heritage will be created, including digital twins of sites and an open data system. Digitization of all heritage sites is planned by 2030.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Fully Digitize Cultural Heritage Sites by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to fully digitize its cultural heritage sites by 2030. Proposals include creating a unified digital platform, digital twins of heritage objects, and an open data system. A situational center will monitor sites using IoT sensors, satellite data, and AI. Visitor management systems will also be implemented.

item.title: ADB delegation reviews Uzbekistan's pharmaceutical sector reforms and potential
item.description: A delegation from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) met with officials from Uzbekistan's Agency for the Development of Medical and Pharmaceutical Industry. They discussed reforms, quality improvement measures, and preparations for joining the Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme (PIC/S). The ADB positively assessed reforms and expressed interest in future collaborations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Fines 22 Banks and 3 Microfinance Organizations
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank imposed fines on 22 banks and 3 microfinance organizations in August for violations. These included non-compliance with prudential norms, legal deviations, and issues found during inspections and mystery shopper controls.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Discuss Further Development of Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov met with Turkey's Deputy Foreign Minister Ayşe Berris Ekinci. They welcomed the results of political consultations and noted the dynamic development of their comprehensive strategic partnership. Discussions also covered current international and regional issues and upcoming bilateral events.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy inventories all international grants
item.description: The Ministry of Economy of Kyrgyzstan is conducting an inventory of all active and completed international grant and technical assistance projects. The ministry aims to improve the efficiency of fund utilization. Deputy Minister Mederbek Tumanov stated that a unified database is being formed to assess project results.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economy Ministry Audits International Grants
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy is conducting an inventory of all active and completed international grant and technical assistance projects. The ministry aims to improve the efficiency of fund utilization by creating a unified database and evaluating project outcomes.

item.title: Central Asian Foreign Ministers Advocate for Strengthening Global Nuclear Security
item.description: Foreign ministers from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan issued a joint statement on the 20th anniversary of the Central Asian Nuclear-Weapon-Free Zone Treaty. They reaffirmed commitment to the treaty's goals, emphasizing its role in regional security and nuclear disarmament, while expressing concern over stalled arms control progress.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Harvests Over 760,000 Tons of Wheat Amid Increased Yields
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has harvested over 760,000 tons of wheat, contributing to a total grain harvest of 1.37 million tons, an increase of 189,700 tons from the previous year. The Ministry of Water Resources and Agriculture reported that average yields rose by 2.8 centners per hectare. Harvesting continues across the country.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Harvests Over 760,000 Tons of Wheat
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has harvested over 760,000 tons of wheat and a total of 1.37 million tons of grain this year, surpassing last year's figures. The Ministry of Agriculture reports higher yields for major crops, with harvesting ongoing and Chuiskaya Oblast leading in grain production.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Produce 1.6 Billion kWh of Electricity Annually from Waste Incineration
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to generate 1.6 billion kWh of electricity annually by incinerating waste. Six investment projects in cooperation with Chinese companies are scheduled for 2026-2027, with a total value of $933 million. This initiative aims to address waste management and energy production.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Expand Participation in International Civil Aviation
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has ratified protocols amending the Convention on International Civil Aviation. These amendments aim to broaden member state representation in ICAO's governing bodies and ensure more balanced regional interests in decision-making. The ratified law establishes a legal framework for increased Uzbek participation in the organization's institutional reforms.

item.title: White House Removes Anti-Immigrant Video Game After Tetris Condemnation
item.description: The White House has removed an anti-immigrant video game, 'Build the Wall,' from its website after it faced criticism, including from Tetris. The game, which resembled Tetris, required players to build a wall on the U.S.-Mexico border. Tetris stated its belief in unity, not division.

item.title: Uzbekistan's National Guard Tasked with Suppressing Mass Riots
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has approved amendments to the National Guard Law, assigning it the new task of suppressing mass riots. This update aims to systematize the Guard's duties, consolidate functions related to public safety and order, and eliminate legislative gaps. The National Guard, established in 2017, has seen its legal status and powers expanded through numerous laws and decrees.
